column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has singular “the field”; BSB uses plural “the fields.” The answer leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies Naomi.
The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed and repeats the root of happening in “her chance happened”; BSB names Ruth and expresses the chance with “happened to come.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the foreman “his young man who was stationed over the reapers”; BSB compresses this into “the foreman of his harvesters.”
The Hebrew explicitly calls her a “Moabite young woman” and describes the territory as Moab’s “field.” BSB has “the Moabitess” and “the land of Moab.”
The Hebrew says she “stood” or remained from morning until now; BSB uses “has continued.” The place of her brief sitting is called “the house,” rendered “the shelter” in BSB.
The Hebrew begins with the question “Have you not heard, my daughter?” BSB changes this to the command “Listen, my daughter.”

The Hebrew asks “Have I not commanded the young men ...?” BSB turns this into “Indeed, I have ordered the young men.” It describes the water as what the young men draw, where BSB describes filled jars.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the explicit time expression “yesterday, the day before yesterday”; BSB renders it as “before.”
The Hebrew wishes that her reward may be “complete”; BSB renders it as “rich” and makes receiving the reward explicit.
The Hebrew says he spoke “to the heart of your maidservant”; BSB renders this bodily expression as “spoken kindly to your maidservant.” It has no separate word for “continue.”
The Hebrew calls the liquid “vinegar”; BSB expands this to “vinegar sauce.” It explicitly mentions “your morsel,” where BSB uses “it” for the bread.
The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed, where BSB supplies her name. The permission to glean among the sheaves is stated directly; BSB frames it as “Even if she gathers.”
The Hebrew emphatically repeats the root of pulling out; BSB uses a single “pull out.”
The Hebrew leaves the woman unnamed; BSB supplies Ruth.
The Hebrew says she gave her what she had left from being satisfied. BSB explicitly supplies “her meal” and identifies the recipient as Naomi.
The Hebrew says she told her mother-in-law about the person with whom she had worked; BSB says she told her “where she had worked.”
The Hebrew explicitly says that the man is “near to us”; BSB calls him “a close relative.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew says to “go out” with his young women; BSB uses “work with.” It describes unnamed people encountering or harming her in another field, where BSB has impersonal “nothing will happen to you.”
The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed and separately names the barley harvest and the wheat harvest; BSB names Ruth and combines the two harvests.
